name: Ahead of It
version: v2 · 2026-11-09 · one app, three lists (was three separate scripts)
verified: 2026-11-09 · Ahead of It v3.0 · 2026-11-08 · every step driven on a phone-sized screen
intro:
⚠️ BEFORE STEP 1 — check you are in a test copy. Look for the small “🧪 Test copy” mark on the screen. It means this app has never seen you, which is what the steps below expect. If it is missing and the app already shows your own information, you have opened your real app: go back to your list and tap this app’s name again, rather than using a bookmark, your history, or an icon on your home screen. Starting in the wrong copy makes the early steps look broken when nothing is wrong.

This used to be three apps — Ahead of It, Ahead of It · Church and Ahead of It · Nonprofit. They are now ONE app with three lists you can turn on and off, so this is the only script for all three. If you tested one of the old ones before, expect things to have moved.

You will work through the example items, delete one, add one of your own, switch the church list on and off, pick from the ready-made library, type a made-up amount of money, print the year, copy the hand-off page, and check it all still works with no internet. Only use the example words and numbers — nothing real, and never a real password.

steps.do: When the app opens, a card sits over the screen: “Welcome to Ahead of It”. Tap the small words “skip the tour” at its bottom right.
steps.see: A new card: “How do you want to start?” with two choices — “🧪 Keep the examples to play with” and “✨ Start fresh with my own”.
steps.tip: A green greeting strip may also show at the top (for example “Good morning.”). Tap its ✕ if it is in the way. A card headed “What am I doing here?” may sit behind — if it is still there later, tap “Got it — let’s go ›” to close it.

steps.do: Tap “🧪 Keep the examples to play with”.
steps.see: The main page, with four example items on it — each one has the word (example) after its name. Near the top a small dark pill says “1 overdue”. The page is in four parts going down: “Overdue”, “Do something now” (with “step is due” on its right), “Next 90 days” and “Later this year”.
steps.tip: Testing again on a phone that has used Ahead of It before? The two welcome cards may not show at all. If you land straight on the list, tick steps 1–2 ✅ and carry on.

steps.do: Under “Overdue” is “Car registration / plates (example)”, a few days overdue. Tap its “step ✓” button.
steps.see: A short note says “Step done ✓”. The grey line under the name changes from “last call → Put the sticker on” to “Do it now”, and the “step ✓” button goes — only “done ✓” is left.

steps.do: On that same “Car registration / plates (example)”, tap “done ✓”.
steps.see: A note says “Done ✓ — next one …” with a date. The “Overdue” box now shows 0 and says “Nothing overdue. That is the whole point.” The car registration has moved down the page with a date about a year away.

steps.do: Tap the NAME “Smoke & CO detector batteries (example)” (the words, not a button).
steps.see: A form slides up with the name already in the “What” box, then “Next due”, “Repeats”, “How bad is it if you miss this?” with three choices, “What happens if you miss it”, “Reminder steps”, “Who else needs to know”, “Amount”, “Where the papers / login are”, “Who to call” and “The papers themselves”. At the very bottom are Save, Cancel and a red Delete.

steps.do: Scroll to the bottom of that form and tap the red “Delete”. A small box asks “Remove this from the list?” — tap OK.
steps.see: The form closes and “Smoke & CO detector batteries (example)” is gone from the list. Nothing else moved.

steps.do: Tap the round orange “＋” button near the bottom right. Then, WITHOUT typing anything, scroll down in the form and tap “Save”.
steps.see: It does not save. A short line says “Give it a name” and the form stays open — an empty item is never added.

steps.do: Scroll back up in the form and type this into the “What” box.
steps.see: Your words read exactly as typed.
steps.tip: There is a small 🎤 button at the right of that box for speaking instead of typing. You do not have to use it — but if you try it and it does nothing, say so.

steps.do: Under “How bad is it if you miss this?” tap “🔴 Costs real money”, then scroll down and tap “Save”.
steps.see: The form closes and your item is on the list under “Do something now”, about 30 days away, with “30 days out → Gather what you need” under it and a red “🔴 costs money” tag.

steps.do: Tap the “📚 Library” tab at the very bottom of the screen.
steps.see: “Showing the list for:” and three buttons — “🏠 Household” (lit up), “⛪ Church” and “💼 Nonprofit” (both dim). Below them, ready-made items in groups: Taxes, Home, Vehicles, Identity, Health, Pets, Money and Business.

steps.do: Tap “⛪ Church”.
steps.see: The church button lights up too — BOTH are now on. Five more groups appear further down: Safety & inspections, Building, Insurance & legal, Money & filings and Seasonal. The household groups are still there; nothing was replaced.
steps.tip: This is the thing we most want tested. These used to be three separate apps, and the whole point of joining them is that a household person who joins a church board does not need a second app. If turning Church on hides your household items, or if the church groups do not appear, that is a serious fault.

steps.do: In the “Safety & inspections” group, tap “Fire extinguisher annual service”.
steps.see: A note says “Added — you are ahead of it. Tap it to fix the date.” The button goes dim and the small print under it now ends with “· added”.

steps.do: Tap “Fire extinguisher annual service” once more.
steps.see: A note says “Already on your list”. It is NOT added a second time.

steps.do: Tap “⛪ Church” to turn it off again. Then tap “🏠 Household” to try to turn that off too.
steps.see: Turning Church off takes its five groups out of the library. Trying to turn the last one off does not work — a note says “Keep at least one” and Household stays lit.

steps.do: Tap the “🧭 Next” tab at the bottom.
steps.see: “Fire extinguisher annual service” is STILL on your list, even though the church list is switched off. Turning a list off only hides the ready-made items — it never takes away something you added.
steps.tip: If your fire extinguisher item has disappeared here, stop and report it straight away. That is the one thing that must never happen.

steps.do: Tap the gold “⚡ Quick setup — tick what’s yours” button near the bottom left. Then, without ticking anything, tap “Save my list — however many that is” at the bottom.
steps.see: A box says “Tick at least one box — or Close if nothing applies today.” Tap OK. The Quick setup screen stays open.

steps.do: Under TAXES tap the box beside “Property tax installment”, then scroll down to IDENTITY and tap the box beside “Passport renewal”.
steps.see: Both boxes get a gold tick ✓. Each row also has a date on its right that you could change.

steps.do: Tap “Save my list — however many that is” at the bottom.
steps.see: A box says “2 items on your list, with dates. That’s a real start. 🌿” Tap OK. The page reloads and both are on the list with their dates.

steps.do: Near the top, tap “💰 Type what’s on hand”. In the box that asks “What is on hand right now — checking plus cash, roughly?” type this number and tap OK.
steps.see: The money strip at the top changes. It now reads “Covered”, with “— $1,250 on hand leaves $1,250 after the bills” under it and today’s date at the end. The button has changed to “💰 Update what’s on hand”.

steps.do: Tap the “🗓 Year” tab at the bottom.
steps.see: Twelve months in a row down the page, this month first. Months with nothing in them show a dash. Your items appear in the right months. At the top it explains the colours: red = costs real money if you miss it, amber = a hassle, green = no big deal.

steps.do: Scroll to the bottom of the Year tab and tap “🖨 Print the year map”.
steps.see: Your phone’s own print or share sheet opens, showing the whole year on one page. You do NOT have to print it — close the sheet and come back. Say whether the page it was about to print looked right.

steps.do: Tap “📅 Add all to my calendar (.ics)”.
steps.see: Your phone either downloads a file or offers to add the dates to your calendar. You do NOT have to add them. Say what your phone actually did — if nothing happened at all, that is a fault.

steps.do: Tap the “🗝 Hand-off” tab at the bottom, then tap “📋 Copy hand-off summary”. Paste it into your notes app to read it.
steps.see: It copied. What you paste is a plain list of every item: when it is due, what happens if you miss it, and who to tell. Everything on your list is in it, including the fire extinguisher you added.

steps.do: Still on the Hand-off tab, tap “⬇ Save backup file”, then scroll to the very bottom of that tab.
steps.see: A file is saved or downloaded. At the very bottom of the tab is the version line: “Ahead of It v3.0 · 2026-11-08 · by Daraja Studio — private by design — no account, no cloud, nothing leaves your phone.”
steps.tip: Do not tap “⬆ Restore backup”, and do not tap “🧹 Start fresh — erase this app’s data” at the bottom of the page. Those wipe the work you have just done.

steps.do: Turn on Airplane Mode (swipe down from the top-right corner, tap ✈️). Tap the “🧭 Next” tab and tap “done ✓” on any item. Then turn Airplane Mode off and pull the page down to reload it (or tap ↻ in Safari).
steps.see: It works with no internet: the item is marked done and moves to its next date. After the reload everything is still there — your fire extinguisher, the two from Quick setup, and the $1,250.

steps.do: Now the videos. This app has 3. Open each one and watch it right through, sound on: Explain it to me — https://jerrywins1.github.io/daraja-apps/shop/watch.html?app=ahead&mode=firsttime  Watch it work — https://jerrywins1.github.io/daraja-apps/shop/watch.html?app=ahead  Train me — https://jerrywins1.github.io/daraja-apps/shop/watch.html?app=ahead&mode=train
steps.see: Each one talks without stopping — no long silences, no sentence starting again. The screen behind the words changes to match what is being said, and when it points at something, that thing is really there. If a video talks about a button or a screen you did not see in this app, say so — that is a real fault and one of the most useful things you can find.
steps.tip: These videos were made after the three apps were joined into one. If any of them still talks about “Ahead of It · Church” or “Ahead of It · Nonprofit” as a separate app you have to buy, that is exactly the kind of thing we need to hear about.

steps.do: Last, the shop page everyone sees before they buy: https://jerrywins1.github.io/daraja-apps/shop/ — find this app on its shelf and read its card.
steps.see: The name, the one-line description and the price all match the app you just used. There is ONE Ahead of It on the shelf, not three. Nothing on the card promises something the app does not do. If the card and the app disagree, the card is the fault — say which bit. That is the end, thank you.
